purpose: Defines the generic principles for writing requirements documents: their responsibility, what to exclude, lifespan, and revision via additive development, used when no project-specific rules exist.
summary: Generic fallback principles applied when no project-specific rules exist
Project-specific rules take priority over these principles
Requirements document responsibility: write what to build from the user viewpoint
Contents: needed features, data, rules, and the value they bring users
Excluded: implementation methods, except already-decided matters with no room for choice
Lifespan is permanent but not immutable
Revision through additive development, with the old document rewritten only after merge
Pointers to the requirement format, spec/design boundary, and additive development specs
tasks: Deciding what belongs in requirements versus design
title: 要件定義書 作成原則
